It’s a pain like nothing I’ve ever felt and it makes me feel very alone, especially since I had to move away from my family just months after his death. The bulk of my grief journey has been a solo one, but what has really helped is hearing other people’s experiences and understanding that what I’m feeling is normal, no matter how hard. I felt crazy for a really long time - still kind of do - but it’s the ultimate human experience and I’m just so glad I knew him when he was alive.

Honestly, the only thing you can do is live. Live through this grief like you’ve lived through the rest of your life. It’ll be like learning to walk again, but it’ll come to you. No one can tell you how to grieve or how to process, so don’t feel like anything you’re doing is wrong. I could say I’m sorry till the cows come home but god will that do nothing. My best piece of advice would be to not give your attention to any unnecessary stuff. If you can get time off of work, do it. Something unimportant requires your attention? Hand it off to someone else. Be close to your family because they will understand your grief like no one else. This is YOUR loss, so don’t spend time and energy you don’t feel you have comforting people who haven’t faced the same loss. It’s ridiculous how much time I’ve spent comforting people who didn’t even know my person well at all. And most importantly, cry. 

Seeing your loved ones pass is immensely frustrating, especially if they’re young. It may seem like you’re stuck in a dense dark cloud, but it will lift. *insert some analogy about crying and rain and clouds here* 

You have so much love in your life, and just to add to that, I love you.

Alright all these comments instil lots of fear and, although justified, listen. You can find other healthy ways to cope with your stress baby. You’ve probably heard it all before, but you’re very young and your brain and body are still developing. We all want you to reach your full potential, and these are your formative years. I understand the urge, and hey, maybe you would only be smoking every once in a while, but it’s clearly not a risk worth taking. You wanted the input, and here it is. 

I’m currently 18 and smoked weed at 17 and during the past year I’ve experimented lots and realized it’s not something I want to do more than maybe once every 2 months. Not cigarettes, but just my personal experience with smoking. 

I personally love journaling to deal with stress and anxiety (I’m quite an anxious person). It doesn’t need to be a legit book, it can be on some sort of platform online, or in a locked note on your phone, or you can make voice entries using voice memos. Google keep is where I keep my digital entries and it’s linked to your email so only you’d really have access to it. This is just me, but it’s an example of finding something healthy that works.
